articles.title: StoneX Retail FX and CFD Revenue Hits Three-Year Low Despite Record Profit
articles.sourceName: Financial And Business News | Finance Magnates
articles.description: StoneX Group's retail FX and CFD revenue fell 15% to $42.4 million in the latest quarter, according to results filed yesterday (Wednesday). That was its lowest quarterly figure in at least three years, based on StoneX's earnings releases. The drop came in a record year for StoneX as a whole. Net income for the 12 months to September 30 rose 72% to $525.4 million on operating revenue of $5.93 billion, helped by a full year of R.J. O'Brien, the US futures broker it agreed to buy in April 2025 for an estimated $900 million. The Self-Directed/Retail segment, home to FOREX.com, was the only one of StoneX's four segments to report lower annual operating revenue. Its share of the total shrank to 6.3% from 9.8%, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation. Clients traded less. Average daily FX and CFD volume in the retail segment fell 17% to $6.15 billion in the quarter, while revenue per million dollars traded was little changed at $106, against $104 a year earlier. Lower volume was also the main reason StoneX gave for a 19% fall in the June quarter, results it published weeks before it retired the City Index brand in the UK. London's trading industry is coming home! Retail Segment Posts a Quarterly Loss After Overhead Before shared costs, the segment's income fell 56% to $6.4 million in the September quarter. After StoneX allocated $15.6 million of overhead to it, the segment reported a loss of $9.2 million, compared with income of $1.9 million a year earlier. Chief Executive Officer Philip Smith said the year brought "record annual performance in our Commercial, Institutional and Payments segments." For the full fiscal year, retail FX and CFD revenue fell 15% to $239.6 million, and the segment's income after overhead dropped 77% to $18.2 million from $79.1 million. The City Index name gave way to StoneX Trading on September 12. Eleven days later, Gain Capital UK, the former City Index Limited, applied to cancel its Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) authorization, leaving StoneX Financial Ltd as the UK entity behind the new brand. In the US, Gain Capital, which runs FOREX.com there, held $204.2 million of retail forex client deposits in August, about 43% of the six-firm total tracked by FM Intelligence from Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) data. Rivals Reported the Same Quarter in Both Directions Other listed CFD brokers, several of them tracked alongside StoneX in FM Intelligence's broker volumes data, reported the same July-September quarter with revenue moving both up and down. At XTB, clients traded 18.3% fewer CFD lots but revenue rose 65.9% as XTB earned almost twice as much per lot, while IG expected OTC net trading revenue about 18% lower as its revenue retention fell to roughly 70% from an average of about 80%. Plus500 reported quarterly revenue up 11% to $203.2 million and said full-year results would beat market expectations. That puts StoneX's 15% fall closer to IG's estimated 18% decline than to the gains at XTB and Plus500. Commercial and Institutional Segments Drive the Record Year Commercial segment operating revenue rose 84% to $1.90 billion for the year, and Institutional rose 40% to $3.45 billion. Listed derivatives revenue doubled to $1.16 billion. The fourth quarter was the weakest of the year. Net income slipped 2% to $84.2 million, below the $127.9 million to $174.3 million of the three previous quarters, and return on equity fell to 11.6% from 15.2%. Securities revenue per million fell 23% in the quarter, which StoneX attributed to narrower spreads in equities and fixed income. Interest and fee income on client balances fell 7% after a $17.9 million unrealized loss on US Treasury and agency holdings. Diluted earnings per share were $0.66 for the quarter and $4.15 for the year, after two three-for-two stock splits in March and July that StoneX applied retroactively to all per-share figures. This article was written by Damian Chmiel at www.financemagnates.com.

articles.title: Look: Emirates' new First Class lounge offers first glimpse of AED 400 million transformation
articles.description: Dubai: Emirates is ushering in a new era of luxury on the ground, unveiling an exquisitely finished First Class Lounge at Concourse B, Terminal 3, Dubai International Airport (DXB). Open to customers from 18 November, the new lounge will welcome First Class customers on a temporary basis for one year before being transformed into a next-generation Business Class Lounge. The opening offers the first glimpse of Emirates' AED 400 million transformation of its flagship lounges, each designed with next-generation features and unmistakable Emirates DNA. Sir Tim Clark, President, Emirates Airline, said, "Our customers expect the very best from Emirates, whether they are flying with us or spending time with us on the ground. We believe the airport experience should be every bit as exceptional as the journey itself, and that's why we are transforming our lounges globally. This new First Class Lounge in Dubai is the first taste of what's to come. And if these are the lengths we will go to for a temporary lounge, just imagine what you can expect from future Emirates lounges. Over the next two years, we'll be unveiling a completely different lounge experience, with new concepts in dining, wellness, entertainment and personalised hospitality. We're going well beyond a traditional refurbishment and creating extraordinary spaces." The future of Emirates Lounges Emirates is undertaking an extensive two-year programme to significantly enhance the lounge experience across Terminal 3, introducing a new generation of premium spaces designed around the evolving needs of today's travellers. As part of the transformation, Emirates is also expanding its lounge footprint at Dubai International Airport (DXB) by introducing a brand-new Business Class Lounge. This will increase the total number of dedicated Emirates lounges in Terminal 3 from seven to eight. From immersive culinary experiences to dedicated wellness facilities and innovative entertainment concepts, Emirates is redefining what customers can expect from their time at the airport. Building on its renowned hospitality, the airline will offer distinct spaces for dining, relaxation, work and socialising, complemented by intuitive technology, refined interiors and elevated personal service. Each lounge will bear the hallmarks of the Emirates brand, with interiors conveying luxury, comfort, exceptional hospitality and global appeal. The investment reinforces Emirates' commitment to delivering an exceptional experience at every stage of the customer journey, both in the air and on the ground. New temporary First Class lounge The first reveal is a beautifully redesigned First Class Lounge in Concourse B, offering customers an exclusive preview of the design philosophy and elevated hospitality concepts that will shape Emirates' next-generation lounges. Created as a luxurious temporary First Class retreat while the wider refurbishment programme is underway, the lounge combines contemporary elegance, comfort and functionality in Emirates' signature palette of gold, bronze and marble, accented with red. Customers can unwind in individual multipurpose seats with built-in chargers, footrests and tables, or settle into quieter corners designed for relaxation. These include chaise longue-style daybeds, blankets, pillows and individual privacy features. For those who wish to work, there is an abundance of tables and dedicated workspaces featuring integrated power outlets and wireless charging, allowing guests to stay seamlessly connected. The dining experience draws inspiration from Dubai's finest and most iconic resorts. Guests can choose from counter seating with sweeping runway views, social and interactive dining tables, and vibrant bar areas. A striking new coffee and cocktail bar, named Brew Bar, offers expertly prepared beverages, while a refreshed culinary experience combines à la carte dining, live cooking, international buffet selections, freshly prepared sushi and Emirates' popular First Class sandwich bar. Every detail has been considered to enhance the pre-flight experience, from elegant new furnishings and ambient lighting to beautifully appointed marble-and-gold shower suites featuring premium VOYA toiletries. Dedicated family facilities, accessible shower suites and inclusive design features ensure a welcoming and comfortable experience for all guests. The new lounge will welcome First Class customers for approximately 12 months before being transformed into an enhanced Business Class facility, coinciding with the opening of Emirates' new First Class Lounge in Concourse B in 2027. Two new next-generation lounges for First Class customers in 2027 The opening marks the beginning of a series of major lounge unveilings. Emirates' First Class Lounge in Concourse C is scheduled to welcome customers in mid-to-late 2027, followed by the redesigned First Class Lounge in Concourse B later in 2027. These flagship spaces will introduce a new dimension to premium airport hospitality, with greater opportunities for privacy, personalisation, wellbeing and indulgence. For customers seeking exclusivity, new prestige VIP suites with private en-suite facilities and dedicated dining rooms will offer intimate retreats away from the main lounge. Wellness will become an integral part of the Emirates lounge experience, with dedicated fitness facilities, spa concepts and relaxation spaces. A new generation of leisure and entertainment areas will further elevate the experience, including a golf simulator, sports lounge and dedicated family and children's spaces. Dining will also take centre stage. New culinary concepts will include Japanese speciality counters with freshly prepared sushi, artisan bakeries and pizza ovens, dessert bars and live cooking experiences. A distinctive 'Made in Dubai' dining concept will celebrate the flavours and culinary heritage of the city alongside premium international cuisine. Customers will also be able to discover curated fine wines at a Le Clos wine cellar, enjoy expertly crafted cocktails and speciality coffees, or indulge in Emirates' exclusive First Class offering, Dom Pérignon Champagne. Two next-generation lounges for Business Class customers over the next two years Emirates' Business Class lounges are also undergoing a sweeping transformation, with the refurbishment of Concourse B introducing a series of new experiences across multiple zones, as well as a brand-new lounge in Concourse C. In Concourse B, the lounge will feature a redesigned reception experience, including dedicated Emirates Skywards service counters, accessible biometric entry gates and a reception area specifically for customers with accessibility requirements. Inside, contemporary interiors will create a seamless transition between vibrant social areas and peaceful quiet zones. New coffee and beverage bars will provide inviting spaces to gather, while the 'Made in Dubai' culinary concept will introduce a fresh celebration of local flavours. Subsequent phases will unveil an expanded selection of live cooking stations, freshly baked bread and pizzas, sushi bars, pasta counters and speciality desserts. The Emirates Moët & Chandon Lounge will also be redesigned, creating a refined new setting for customers to discover exclusive champagne and canapé pairings. Further enhancements will continue through 2027 and 2028, introducing new culinary concepts and upgraded dining and hospitality facilities. The new lounge concept will also pay tribute to Dubai through locally inspired design elements and artwork that celebrate the city's heritage and cultural identity. A specially commissioned collection by artist Tina Ahmed, entitled The Dubai Heritage Collection, draws inspiration from the city's history before its iconic skyline, when life was shaped by the Creek, the sea and the desert. In Concourse C, a brand-new Emirates Business Class Lounge will offer a sophisticated, residential-inspired environment. Signature design features will include Rolex clocks displaying global time zones, a striking Ghaf tree honouring the UAE's cultural heritage and a light-filled Botanical Glass Atrium showcasing lush greenery to create a calming sense of tranquillity. The spacious lounge will offer a variety of comfortable leather seating options, including semi-enclosed individual seats, banquettes, two- and four-seater loungers, and communal spaces for working and socialising. Universal charging points and wireless chargers will be available at every seat. Guests can also refresh in luxurious, spa-inspired shower suites and dedicated prayer rooms. A wide range of new culinary attractions for Business Class guests will include freshly prepared international and regional dishes, an authentic Arabic mezze bar, a dedicated Noodle Bar serving made-to-order dishes, a Dim Sum station offering freshly steamed delicacies, and convenient self-service tea and coffee stations. A new Brew Bar will celebrate global coffee culture with speciality coffees, alongside Emirates' signature selection of champagne, cocktails and beers. Designed for every traveller, at every stage of the journey Across the refurbishment programme, Emirates is placing greater emphasis on accessibility, convenience and individual customer needs. Enhanced facilities will include wheelchair-accessible reception counters and biometric gates, dedicated reception areas, accessible shower suites and washrooms, and inclusive private lounge spaces. For travellers seeking peace and quiet, carefully designed relaxation zones will provide comfortable seating, soft lighting and an atmosphere conducive to rest. Dedicated nursing and mother-and-baby facilities, family areas and children's playrooms will also offer greater comfort and flexibility for customers travelling with young children. The transformation reflects Emirates' focus on creating lounges that adapt to the individual needs of its customers, whether they have just minutes before departure or several hours between flights. Investing in the Emirates experience worldwide The AED 400 million transformation of Emirates' Dubai lounges builds on the airline's wider investment in next-generation airport hospitality across its global network. Emirates currently operates 34 dedicated lounges at international airports, in addition to its flagship facilities in Dubai. Its new signature lounge design has already been introduced in destinations including Munich, Frankfurt and Manchester, bringing the airline's latest premium hospitality concepts to customers around the world. With the addition of the new Concourse C facility, Emirates' dedicated lounge network will expand to 42 lounges worldwide, including eight at Dubai International Airport. Emirates lounges are available to eligible First Class and Business Class customers, as well as Emirates Skywards Platinum and Gold members. Paid access is also offered, subject to availability.
